summary: Steel 100-ft fire lookout completed about one mile east of Chadbourn by August 1931; no source read describes its later history or the site today.

facts.design: Steel tower, 100 ft, with an inside stairway and an enclosed lookout cabin at the top
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Completed by August 1931 about one mile east of Chadbourn on State Highway 20. The May 1930 plan had put it about two miles east.

evidence.supports: May 13, 1930 announcement, by the Department of Conservation and Development, of a tower in the western part of Columbus County
evidence.quote: the latest unit to be constructed in the western part of Columbus County near Chadbourn, it was announced yesterday at the Department of Conservation and Development.

evidence.supports: 1930 plan: tower probably about two miles east of Chadbourn
evidence.quote: the tower will probably be placed about two miles east of Chadbourn.

evidence.supports: Planned design: steel, 100 feet, inside stairway
evidence.quote: The structure will be of steel construction, 100 feet in height and will have an inside stairway.

evidence.supports: Planned enclosed lookout cabin at the top
evidence.quote: A station for a fire lookout will be in an enclosed cabin at the top of the shaft.

evidence.supports: Planned view of about 15 miles in all directions
evidence.quote: The lookout will have a range of vision of about 15 miles radius in all directions.

evidence.supports: Completion report dated August 4, 1931 (The Bee): one mile east of Chadbourn on State Highway 20
evidence.quote: The erection of a 100-foot high steel forest fire observation tower near state highway number twenty, one mile east of Chadbourn has been completed.

evidence.supports: 22nd unit in a proposed state-wide system of 125
evidence.quote: It is the 22nd unit in a proposed state-wide system of 125.

evidence.supports: Site given to the state by C.R. Bailey
evidence.quote: The site of the tower was given to the State by C.R. Bailey, of Chadbourn.
North Carolina - Columbus County - North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1930 plan put the tower about two miles east of Chadbourn. The August and September 1931 reports say the finished tower is about one mile east on State Highway 20. The story uses the finished location.

notes_for_editor: All history comes from one page that reprints three 1930-31 newspaper items (The Charlotte News, The Bee, The Forest Worker); the story cites the page. The May 1930 article describes the Department of Conservation and Development as the body announcing the tower, while the page header names the NC Division of Forest Resources as agency; both are kept as stated. Brief coordinates (34.3248, -78.8084) differ by about 5 km from the NC tower list entry for Chadbourn (34.27916, -78.81527, tnlandforms.us). The brief point was kept because the 1931 reports place the tower about one mile east of town, but no fetched source checks either point on a map, so an editor should verify. Status, access, staffing and fate: no source read says anything, so none are written. A digitalnc photo record (lib.digitalnc.org/record/18660) returned no text, so no photo is added.
